source_units.complete_text: When the Heavenly One distinguishes kings upon it, they will be covered with snow in Selmon.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Selmon and snow after the heavenly One distinguishes kings do not establish the proposed identification with Abimelech's wood-cutting mountain. The named-place candidate remains uncredited.

source_units.complete_text: A mountain of God, a rich mountain; a curdled mountain, a rich mountain.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The rich and curdled mountain is preserved without replacing it with an unexpressed mountain name or deciding which physical mountain the description denotes.

source_units.complete_text: Blessed is the Lord day by day; the God of our salvations will prosper our way. Diapsalma.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Daily blessing and the God of salvations do not furnish a specific independent connection beyond a broad praise-and-salvation formula.

source_units.complete_text: The Lord said, “I will return from Bashan; I will return in the depths of the sea,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Lord says I will return from Bashan and I will return in the depths of the sea. The line is not rewritten as bringing enemies back, and the identity or occasion of this return is unresolved.

source_units.complete_text: Thy processions were seen, God, the processions of my God, the King in the holy place.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The divine King's processions in the holy place do not establish the particular ark procession in Chronicles. That historical identification remains a zero-credit candidate.

source_units.complete_text: There is Benjamin, the younger, in ecstasy; Judah’s rulers, their leaders, Zebulun’s rulers, Naphtali’s rulers.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Benjamin, Judah, Zebulun and Naphtali are named in this gathering, but no particular historical tribal assembly is identified by these names alone.

source_units.complete_text: Command Thy power, God; strengthen, God, this which Thou didst accomplish for us.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The petition that God command His power and strengthen what He accomplished for the community does not identify a particular act or army.

source_units.complete_text: Give glory to God; His magnificence is over Israel, and His power in the clouds.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Giving glory to God, His magnificence upon Israel and His power in clouds are not combined into a retained match on the strength of a general glory command alone.

source_units.complete_text: Attend to my soul and redeem it; because of my enemies, rescue me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Attending to the soul and redeeming because of enemies is not assigned an independent target merely from common redemption-and-enemy language.

source_units.complete_text: For Thou knowest my reproach, shame and embarrassment; all those afflicting me are before Thee.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: God's knowledge of reproach, shame and the people afflicting the speaker who are before Him remains this lament; it does not identify a separate trial scene or a particular historical group.

source_units.complete_text: Add lawlessness to their lawlessness, and let them not enter Thy righteousness.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The request to add lawlessness to lawlessness and bar entry into divine righteousness is not flattened into an ordinary forgiveness or judgment formula.

source_units.complete_text: I am poor and in pain, and the salvation of Thy presence, God, supported me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Poverty, pain and the declaration that the salvation of God's presence supported the speaker have no retained independent link more particular than a general suffering-and-rescue theme.

source_units.complete_text: I will praise God’s name with a song and magnify Him in praise,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Magnifying and praising God's name in song is preserved without retaining a generic praise verse solely because it shares that activity.

source_units.complete_text: For Thou art my endurance, Lord; the Lord is my hope from my youth.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Hope in the Lord from youth is not assigned a separate counterpart on the basis of lifelong trust alone; the more concrete womb language in the following unit has its own retained comparison.

source_units.complete_text: I became like a portent to the many, and Thou art a mighty helper.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Being a portent to many and having God's strong help do not identify the particular sign-children in Isaiah or another named portent.

source_units.complete_text: Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that I may sing of Thy glory, Thy majesty all day.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: A mouth filled with praise throughout the day is not given a separate target through a general continual-praise theme alone.

source_units.complete_text: But I will always hope, and add to all Thy praise.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Continued hope and addition to praise remain this speaker's resolve without an independently established specific relationship.

source_units.complete_text: I will enter in the Lord’s power; Lord, I will remember Thy righteousness alone.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The proposed Isaiah comparison does not contain the expected righteousness-and-strength formula in this pinned text. The psalm's entry in God's power and remembrance of His righteousness alone remain pending rather than supported by an outside-edition wording.

source_units.complete_text: Thou didst teach me, God, from my youth, and until now I will announce Thy wonders.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The teaching from youth and the unusual clause 'until now I will announce Thy wonders' are preserved without normalizing their temporal wording. No separate counterpart is established by general instruction and praise language; the following explicit future-generation purpose has a distinct retained comparison.

source_units.complete_text: Let the mountains take up peace for Thy people, and the hills in righteousness.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Mountains taking up peace and hills righteousness are not identified with named rulers or transformed into an ordinary agricultural blessing.

source_units.complete_text: He will spare the poor and needy, and save the souls of the needy.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Sparing the poor and saving the needy's souls is retained as the royal portrait, without an additional target supported only by general mercy toward the poor.

source_units.complete_text: for there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourging.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The actual clause concerns no refusal at their death and firmness in scourging. It is not rewritten as painless death or bodily health, and its precise connection remains unsettled.

source_units.complete_text: Their injustice will come out as though from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Injustice coming out as from fat and passing into a disposition of heart are preserved. A familiar eyes-bulging paraphrase would change the evidence, so no match based on it is retained.

source_units.complete_text: They devised and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice against the height.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source says injustice spoken against the height, without explicitly naming that height as God or the Most High. The checked Daniel passage explicitly names the Most High; the uncertain identification is not retained as a supported match.

source_units.complete_text: They set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The mouth set toward heaven and tongue passing over earth form a specific spatial image; general arrogant-speech similarities do not establish a particular counterpart for this whole image.

source_units.complete_text: Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The returning people, their destination here and their full days remain unclear in this clause. No referents or return event are supplied from another text.

source_units.complete_text: and I became scourged all day, and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker is scourged all day and rebuked in the mornings. The checked Job passage has morning visitation and judgment for rest, not this precise combination, so the proposal remains pending.

source_units.complete_text: If I were saying, “I will recount it thus,” behold, I would have broken faith with the generation of Thy sons.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker restrains an account because it would break faith with the generation of God's sons. No independently supported counterpart for that precise restraint and obligation is retained.

source_units.complete_text: until I enter God’s sanctuary and understand their last things.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Entering the sanctuary changes understanding of the sinners' last things. Generic sanctuary or judgment language alone has not established a sufficiently particular independent match.

source_units.complete_text: For my heart was set ablaze, and my kidneys were altered,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The heart is set ablaze and kidneys altered in the source wording. An imported embittered-heart rendering would replace the evidence, and no secure counterpart for the actual formulation is retained.

source_units.complete_text: For what is there for me in heaven? And what did I desire from Thee upon the earth?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The two questions about heaven and desire from God on earth are preserved without rewriting them as a simple declaration that God is the only desire. A sufficiently precise counterpart is unresolved.

source_units.complete_text: As though into the entrance above,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This short unit is the fragment As though into the entrance above. Its attachment to surrounding destruction imagery is retained without manufacturing a full independent proposition or target.

source_units.complete_text: I said to those acting lawlessly, “Do not act lawlessly,” and to those sinning, “Do not raise a horn;
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The prohibition of lawlessness and raising a horn is preserved. The checked Hannah warning names boastful speech rather than horn-raising in this particular verse; a broad self-exaltation analogy is insufficient for a retained match.

source_units.complete_text: For neither from the goings-out nor from the settings, nor from desert mountains,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The directions and desert-mountains fragment is preserved as supplied. Promotion or exaltation is not inserted as an absent noun to create a conventional match.

source_units.complete_text: For the end, among hymns. A psalm of Asaph; a song concerning the Assyrian.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The heading explicitly says concerning the Assyrian, but does not identify a king, battle or date. The checked Assyrian defeat account remains a proposed occasion with no completion credit.

source_units.complete_text: All those without understanding in heart were troubled; they slept their sleep, and all the men of wealth found nothing with their hands.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The actual line combines uncomprehending hearts, sleep and men of wealth finding nothing with their hands. It is not converted into a conventional slain-warriors translation.

source_units.complete_text: From heaven Thou didst cause judgment to be heard; the earth feared and grew quiet,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The earth fears and grows quiet after judgment is heard from heaven. The checked Habakkuk line commands reverence, not silence; the full proposed correspondence is not established.

source_units.complete_text: For human thought will acknowledge Thee, and the remainder of thought will keep a feast for Thee.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The verse says human thought will acknowledge God and the remainder of thought will keep a feast for Him. It is not changed to a familiar human-wrath formulation, and the actual thought-and-feast relation remains unresolved.

source_units.complete_text: And I said, “Now I have begun; this is the change of the Most High’s right hand.”
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Now I have begun and the change of the Most High's right hand are retained. No different translation's anguish or remembrance reading is substituted to resolve the statement.

source_units.complete_text: The sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting bows, turned back on the day of war.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Ephraim's archers turn back on a day of war. The checked Chronicles family deaths do not state archery or retreat and do not identify this battle.

source_units.complete_text: Fire devoured their young men, and their virgins were not mourned.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source says fire devoured young men and virgins were not mourned. A familiar virgins-not-married rendering would change the text; no secure independent match for the actual two clauses is retained.

source_units.complete_text: and struck His enemies backward; He gave them everlasting reproach.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The enemies are struck backward and receive perpetual reproach. The checked ark judgment names bodily affliction differently and does not establish this exact backward-striking clause.

source_units.complete_text: Her shadow covered mountains, and her climbing branches covered God’s cedars.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The vine shades mountains and covers God's cedars with climbing branches. No location or people represented by each landscape feature is established, and generic vine growth is insufficient.

source_units.complete_text: A pig from the woodland ravaged her, and a solitary wild beast grazed her down.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The woodland pig and solitary wild beast ravage the vine. No particular nation or ruler is identified by these animals, and a general vineyard-destruction parallel does not resolve their specific imagery.

source_units.complete_text: He established it as a testimony in Joseph, when he went out from the land of Egypt; a language he did not know, he heard.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The testimony in Joseph, departure from Egypt and hearing an unknown language retain ambiguous pronoun subjects and occasion. The checked Exodus departure text does not resolve those subjects or identify this observance.

source_units.complete_text: A song of a psalm for Asaph.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This unit contains the song-and-psalm attribution to Asaph. The general heading alone did not establish a particular literary relationship or an identifiable occasion; no historical Asaph identity was inferred.

source_units.complete_text: the dwellings of the Idumeans, and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarenes,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The native coalition-list unit names Idumeans, Ishmaelites, Moab and Hagarenes. Its precise coalition and occasion are not established by the differently composed force in the read Chronicles account; the proposed historical identification remains a separate unretained candidate.

source_units.complete_text: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, and foreigners with those who inhabit Tyre.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This continuation names Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, foreigners and Tyre inhabitants. No sufficiently particular account identifying this combination and its counsel was established; shared people names or generic warfare alone would not identify the episode.

source_units.complete_text: in the valley of weeping, toward a place which he appointed; for the lawgiver will also give blessings.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The actual continuation has the valley of weeping, movement toward an appointed place and blessings given by the lawgiver. No sufficiently particular counterpart to this combination was established; familiar springs or rainfall were not supplied to replace the wording.

source_units.complete_text: Lord, God of powers, hear my prayer; give ear, God of Jacob. Diapsalma.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit asks the Lord God of powers and God of Jacob to hear prayer. A particular relationship beyond these common divine addresses and an ordinary request for hearing was not established in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: For the end. A psalm for the sons of Korah.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source is the general heading for the end and for the sons of Korah. Its broad attribution and designation alone do not establish a particular occasion or a sufficiently distinctive heading comparison.

source_units.complete_text: A prayer for David. Incline Thine ear, Lord, and hear me, for I am poor and needy.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The heading names a prayer for David and the petition asks hearing because the speaker is poor and needy. No particular Davidic episode or sufficiently specific counterpart beyond the widespread hearing-and-need formula was established.

source_units.complete_text: Have mercy on me, Lord, for unto Thee I will cry all day.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This unit requests mercy and promises crying to God all day. A sufficiently particular correspondence beyond that common petition and duration was not established; an unexpressed occasion was not assigned.

source_units.complete_text: Give ear, Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my petition.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source asks God to give ear to the prayer and attend to the voice of petition. No sufficiently particular relationship beyond the ordinary vocabulary of requesting divine hearing was established in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: I will remember Raab and Babylon to those who know me. And look: foreigners and Tyre and the people of Ethiopians— these were born there.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Raab, Babylon, foreigners, Tyre and Ethiopians appear with a statement that these were born there. The antecedent and identities needed for a particular historical or birth-register comparison remain uncertain; Raab was not silently renamed Egypt and the birthplace was not supplied.

source_units.complete_text: Let my prayer enter before Thee; incline Thine ear to my petition, Lord.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The petition asks that prayer enter before God and that He incline His ear. No particular correspondence beyond common language for a prayer being received was established, and the speaker or occasion was not identified from the heading.

source_units.complete_text: I am poor and in toils from my youth; but after being raised up, I was humbled and left helpless.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker describes poverty and toils from youth and says that after being raised up he was humbled and left helpless. No particular counterpart to that actual sequence was established; a royal biography or a different order of exaltation and humiliation was not supplied.

source_units.complete_text: Of understanding; of Ethan the Israelite.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The heading identifies understanding and Ethan the Israelite without ancestry or an occasion. The independently read Ethan and Gaithan entries do not resolve which person is intended; those proposed identities are separately preserved at zero credit.

source_units.complete_text: Lord, God of powers, who is like Thee? Thou art mighty, Lord, and Thy truth surrounds Thee.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit combines an address to the Lord God of powers, a question of incomparability, divine might and surrounding truth. No additional particular relationship beyond these broad praise expressions was established; surrounding truth was not changed into a different attribute.

source_units.complete_text: with which Thine enemies reproached, Lord, with which they reproached the exchange of Thine anointed.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The enemies reproach the exchange of the anointed. The meaning of exchange and the precise object of the reproach remain unresolved; the read mockery of Jesus does not establish the proposed identification or justify replacing exchange with footsteps.

source_units.complete_text: Do not turn a man toward humiliation; and Thou saidst, Return, sons of men.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The negative request not to turn a man toward humiliation and the following call to return are preserved. Genesis names return to earth, but this unit does not; the proposed mortality-image identification remains pending.

source_units.complete_text: For we failed in Thine anger and were troubled in Thy wrath.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The community failed in divine anger and was troubled in wrath. No particular historical judgment is identified by those general experiences, even within the Moses-attributed prayer.

source_units.complete_text: For all our days failed, and in Thine anger we failed; I pondered our years like a spider.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The years are pondered like a spider in the supplied text. This is not replaced with a sigh or an assumed web, and the read Bildad candidate describes a different spider-web construction.

source_units.complete_text: So make known how to number Thy right hand, and those bound in heart in wisdom.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The line asks how to number Thy right hand and refers to those bound in heart in wisdom. It is not rewritten as a request to number our days to create a familiar cross-reference.

source_units.complete_text: Look upon Thy servants and Thy works, and guide their children.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The servants, God's works and guidance of their children are preserved. No identified episode or sufficiently particular separate counterpart for this combination is established.

source_units.complete_text: Let the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct the works of our hands for us.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Splendor upon the community and direction of the work of its hands remain the petition. The expected Proverbs 16:3 unit is absent in this edition, and a general work-and-blessing theme does not establish an alternative precise relation.

source_units.complete_text: the thing passing through darkness, the calamity and the demon of noon.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The thing passing through darkness, calamity and demon of noon are kept as supplied. No target identifies that noon demon or warrants replacing the language with an expected pestilence formulation.

source_units.complete_text: A thousand will fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The stated thousand and ten thousand falling on different sides do not identify a particular battle or plague. The assurance is not assigned a narrative solely from its general protection motif.

source_units.complete_text: A psalm of a song, for the Sabbath day.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Sabbath designation supplies no named performance or performers. The read Levitical-service candidate does not identify this particular song as the one performed.

source_units.complete_text: A senseless man will not know, and one without understanding will not understand these things:
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The senseless person's inability to understand points forward to the following account of wicked flourishing and destruction. No separate link is retained merely from a general ignorance-and-wisdom contrast.

source_units.complete_text: But Thou art Most High for ever, Lord.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The everlasting Most High confession is preserved without adding a separate target on the basis of the general divine-exaltation theme alone.

source_units.complete_text: My eye looked upon my enemies, and my ear will hear of evildoers rising against me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The eye looked upon enemies and the ear will hear of evildoers rising against the speaker. Their downfall is not inserted into either sensory statement to create a triumph correspondence.

source_units.complete_text: utter and speak injustice— will all who work lawlessness speak?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The continuing question about uttering injustice and the speech of workers of lawlessness does not provide a more particular independent counterpart than the common theme of wrongful speech.

source_units.complete_text: Understand now, you senseless among the people; and you fools, become wise at last.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The call for senseless people to understand and fools to become wise is retained as the transition to the creator-of-senses argument. A generic wisdom invitation is insufficient for a separate supported pair.

source_units.complete_text: Will the One who disciplines nations not rebuke— the One who teaches humankind knowledge?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The question about the discipliner of nations and teacher of human knowledge is preserved. No separate link is assigned from divine teaching or rebuke as a broad theme.

source_units.complete_text: to soothe him from evil days, until a pit is dug for the sinner.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The soothing from evil days until a pit is dug for the sinner does not state who digs it. It is not equated with a wrongdoer falling into his own trap, and no sufficiently precise independent comparison is retained.

source_units.complete_text: until righteousness returns to judgment, and all the upright in heart cling to it. Diapsalma.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Righteousness returning to judgment and upright hearts clinging to it are kept in their supplied construction. An ordinary justice-and-righteousness theme does not resolve the precise temporal and relational wording.

source_units.complete_text: Who will rise for me against evildoers, or who will stand beside me against workers of lawlessness?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The questions about an ally rising and standing against evildoers identify no historical helper or particular encounter. General requests for assistance do not provide a sufficiently distinct match.

source_units.complete_text: Lord, amid the multitude of pains in my heart, Thy consolations loved my soul.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The pains in the heart and consolations loving the soul are preserved without replacing the latter verb with a familiar delight formulation. A general divine-comfort passage is not retained on that theme alone.

source_units.complete_text: Come, let us bow down and fall before Him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The combined summons to bow, fall and weep before the Maker is preserved. Weep is not changed to kneel, and a generic worship command alone is not an independent specific counterpart.

source_units.complete_text: The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all the peoples.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Divine greatness in Zion and exaltation above peoples are preserved without adding another pair merely from the broad Zion-praise theme.

source_units.complete_text: A crooked heart did not cling to me; when the evil one turned away from me, I did not know him.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The crooked heart did not cling, and the evil one turned away from the speaker, who did not know him. These agents and past forms are not replaced by a general future resolve to avoid evil.

source_units.complete_text: Hear my prayer, Lord, and let my cry come unto Thee.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The request that God hear a prayer and receive its cry remains unlinked because that common prayer-opening formula supplies no further distinctive correspondence here.

source_units.complete_text: I stayed awake and became like a little bird alone on a roof.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Wakefulness and a little bird alone on a roof are preserved. The read Proverbs candidate describes a bird flying down from its nest and an estranged person's enslavement; it does not establish the same solitary-rooftop image.

source_units.complete_text: All day my enemies reproached me, and those praising me swore against me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Enemies reproached the speaker and those praising him swore against him. The unusual praising and swearing roles are not rewritten as raging enemies or an unstated use of his name as a curse.

source_units.complete_text: He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our lawless deeds,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source explicitly denies treatment or repayment according to sins. Ezra 9:13 says God lightened lawless deeds and gave deliverance, but does not expressly describe a lesser punishment. That proposed punitive equivalence remains uncredited; no sufficiently particular supported alternative is retained.

source_units.complete_text: Mountains rise and plains descend to the place Thou didst found for them.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The rising mountains and descending plains reach their founded place. Genesis 8:5 describes mountain tops appearing as floodwaters recede, not mountains rising and plains descending. Identifying these scenes requires a claim the read texts do not establish.

source_units.complete_text: They give drink to all the beasts of the field; wild donkeys will receive it for their thirst.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Animals drinking and wild donkeys quenching thirst are stated specifically. A general account of wild donkeys or divine food provision would not establish a particular independent drinking comparison; none is retained.

source_units.complete_text: Upon them the birds of heaven will nest; from among the rocks they will give voice.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source combines birds nesting upon them with a voice from rocks. The antecedent and a sufficiently particular independent counterpart remain unsettled. The actual rock wording is preserved instead of supplying a tree-branch clause.

source_units.complete_text: The sun rose, and they gathered, and they will lie down in their enclosures.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The sunrise-associated gathering and lying in enclosures is distinct from the creatures lying in ambush in Job 38:40. A generic shelter or animal-rest association does not establish the particular daylight pattern here.
